Alleged ‘green lounge’ plan by Cat Matlala at OR Tambo sparks national security fears

South Africa has narrowly avoided what investigators describe as a potential national security breach following revelations that controversial businessman and accused criminal Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala allegedly pursued plans to establish a luxury private terminal at OR Tambo International Airport.

According to investigative reports by News24 and Eyewitness News, the proposal, known as the “Green Lounge,” had reached an advanced planning stage and envisioned a fully functioning private terminal that would allow selected clients to fast-track immigration and customs processes.

The plan raised alarm because it would have placed security screening at a national key point in the hands of Matlala’s private agents.

The scheme reportedly included a R70 million-a-year funding pitch to Nedbank, framed as an exclusive service for ultra-wealthy clients.

However, concerns intensified due to Matlala’s criminal profile and alleged links to drug cartels, prompting warnings that the project could have compromised border control and national security.

Matlala is currently detained in a super maximum security prison in Kokstad and faces multiple serious charges, including attempted murder, fraud, and conspiracy to commit murder.

The revelations have reignited debate over governance, oversight, and how individuals with serious criminal allegations can gain proximity to critical state infrastructure.
